name: Flash & EEPROM Wear Lifetime
blurb: how long flash, EEPROM emulation or a log area lasts at a write rate, with wear levelling
intro: Counts how many record writes an area survives before its busiest sector reaches the rated erase cycles - in place, as a circular log, as ST EEPROM emulation, under littlefs or behind an eMMC/SSD controller - and turns that into years at your write interval, with the formula and what each change buys.

inputs.label: Erase cycles (endurance)
inputs.help: From the datasheet; empty = the technology's typical value.

inputs.label: Bytes per write
inputs.help: One record / EEPROM element as stored (address + data + CRC).

inputs.label: Live variables
inputs.help: Distinct variables copied on every page transfer.

examples.title: STM32L4 EEPROM emulation: 4 x 2 KiB pages, 50 variables, a write every 5 s
Data logger on a 16 MiB SPI NOR with littlefs, 64-byte records every 10 s, half full

usage: Give tech, endurance (cycles; empty = typical), eraseSize, areaSize and recordSize in bytes, interval in seconds between writes, scheme (none, circular, eeprom, littlefs, ftl) with variables (eeprom) or fill % (littlefs), wa (write amplification) and target years. Returns the lifetime, writes to wear-out, how many sectors actually wear, erases per day, a sensitivity table (interval, area, record size, WA, endurance) and the formula with the numbers filled in. Use it to size an EEPROM-emulation area, a log partition or a write rate before it ships.
sources: ST AN3969 'EEPROM emulation in STM32F40x/STM32F41x microcontrollers' (page transfer, two-page scheme)
ST AN4894 'EEPROM emulation techniques and software for STM32 microcontrollers' (element format, N pages, cycling capability)
littlefs DESIGN.md, 'Wear leveling' (dynamic wear levelling over free blocks, block_cycles)
JEDEC JESD84-B51 eMMC (device-managed wear levelling, EXT_CSD life time estimation)
Datasheets for typical endurance: STM32F407 (10 kcycles, retention vs cycles), Winbond W25Q128JV (100 kcycles, 20 years), Microchip 24LC256 (1 Mcycles)
